blocks.text: India's Civilian Awards recognize outstanding contributions in various fields, including arts, literature, science, public service, and social work. These awards are announced every year on Republic Day (26th January) and are conferred by the President of India at Rashtrapati Bhavan.
1. Bharat Ratna (Highest Civilian Award)
Eligibility: Any individual, irrespective of nationality.
Instituted in: 1954
Total recipients till date: 53 (as of 2024)
Firstrecipient:C. Rajagopalachari, Dr.S. Radhakrishnan, and Dr. C.V. Raman (1954)
First female recipient: Indira Gandhi (1971)
First posthumous recipient: Lal Bahadur Shastri (1966)
First sportsperson recipient: Sachin Tendulkar (2014)
(Also the Youngest recipient: at age 40)
Non-Indian recipients: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1987), Nelson Mandela (1990)

India's Gallantry Awards are presented to military personnel and civilians for acts of bravery and valor in the face of extreme danger. These awards are divided into wartime gallantry awards and peacetime gallantry awards.
1. Wartime Gallantry Awards
Param Vir Chakra (Highest Wartime Gallantry Award)
Mahavir Chakra (Second-Highest)
Vir Chakra (Third-Highest)
2. Peacetime Gallantry Awards
Ashoka Chakra (Highest Peacetime Gallantry Award)
Kirti Chakra (Second-Highest)
Shaurya Chakra (Third-Highest)

Instituted: 1901 by the Nobel Foundation (Sweden!/ Norway)
6 Categories: Peace, Literature, Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Economics Nobel prize is given in the memory of Alfred Nobel (discoverer of Dynamite)
All Nobel prize is awarded in Stockholm, Sweden while Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.
First Recipient:
Wilhelm Conrad Réntgen (Physics, 1901) - for the discovery of X-rays.
First female recipient:
Marie Curie (1903) - Only woman to win 2 Nobel:
Shared 1st Nobel with her husband Pierre Curie & Henri Becquerel.
Won 2nd Nobel in 1911 for the discovery of Radium & Polonium.
First Indian Recipient:
Rabindranath Tagore (Literature) 1913 for Geetanjali.
